Solar panels and a Starlink system on a lagoon float run an AI salmon counter at Redoubt Lake, 15 miles by boat from Sitka.

Fish and Game put the Redoubt annual subsistence limit at 100 sockeye per household effective July 1st. Jeff Feldpausch of the Sitka Tribe told KCAW it was 50 before, and that the weir is why.

A federal grant titled "Artificial Intelligence for Subsistence Salmon Monitoring and Management" paid $200,000 to install the system. That was installation money. Feldpausch told KCAW there is no funding for the weir right now. Every grant source the Tribe found deals with systems needing remediation.

The deck has the grant title in full, weir counts from 2023 to 2025, and the accuracy number he gave the radio.

What would this weir have to break before a grant program could see it?

#AlaskaSalmon #SubsistenceFishing #WeirCounts

Editor's note

GAS WATCH: PASS, read 2026-08-08, 7 days on record, chart present, checker clean. The daily read caught one prose defect and fixed it in presentation only. The page had been publishing a ratio-to-demand as a share of the region's gas, which read as 134.1 percent of it on an injection day. The explaining clause is now computed from the sign of the measured withdrawal. Collector, model config and both gas ledgers untouched.

SCORE: 8.02 against the 8.0 threshold for three revision rounds. Zero hard fails. It cleared by 0.02 and nothing scored above 8, so this is a pass and not a comfortable one.

TWO REPAIRS MADE AFTER THE SCORE. Slide 08's leader was labelled ADIPOSE FIN but anchored on the dorsal contour toward the head, and the adipose fin sits back near the tail. The scorer could not resolve the fish's orientation from the render and flagged it. Alaskans will know, so the anatomical claim is dropped rather than guessed and the callout now reads THE FISH IN FOCUS. Slide 03's faintest string was lifted to full white.

SOURCING CAVEAT: the Daily Sitka Sentinel blocks direct fetching, so its Redoubt reporting was read through the Ketchikan Daily News reprint. Salmon Vision's published model metric is deliberately absent from every slide and from the caption, struck at the storyboard level by unanimous director agreement, so the two incommensurable accuracy figures can never meet.

ONE THING NEEDING YOUR CALL. Four of six scouts led with the Anthropic employees' $372,000 to a candidate for governor, plainly the loudest Alaska AI story of the week. It was ruled out because this page already ran it on July 25th and again on July 31st, and the July 31st deck disclosed on its own cover that it was the second in seven days. It is also this publication's own maker, which is a judgement that belongs to you rather than to an unattended run. Say the word and a future run will cover the backlash with the same disclosure protocol the two earlier decks used.

CAPTION ROOM: candidate A won with the critic's one fix installed, a NEW:ELIGIBILITY TEST close replacing a burned who-decides. The critic caught candidate B's close as the burned PRICE frame in new wording, and caught an absence claim the record does not support. Both directors flagged their own assigned closing moves as burned against the ledger, unprompted.

REVIEW: five pixel critics, one flow critic, three scoring cycles. The flow critic caught the deck's spine number resetting to zero on its own turn frame, which five pixel critics had all missed. Two cycles were capped at 6.90 by layout collisions the machine gates rated as warns.

Automation changes this run (3)

The routine modified its own machinery this run. If a later week looks worse, this dated section is the rollback trail (each set reverts as one commit).
KindChangeRollback
fix
engine		AN ENCODING PROBE MUST NOW SAY WHICH WAY IT READS, AND THE ENGINE CHECKS THE SLIDE AGAINST ITS OWN DECLARATION. `data-encodes` gains a required `reads` of "differ" (the two regions must be tellable apart) or "same" (an absence or sameness claim); qa.py FAILS a declaration that omits it or uses an unknown word, and FAILS a "differ" whose two regions are under ENC_DIFFER_MIN_DE (4.0 dE) apart at 432px feed width. This is NOT the quality threshold the 2026-07-29 calibration rejected and does not revisit it: the known-bad from that calibration (the steel-below-brass column, dE 49.0) still passes here, correctly, because this asks only whether the probe measured anything at all. No threshold is drawn for "same", because the corpus has no known-bad for that direction to fit one against. Opt-in preserved: a slide that declares no encoding is untouched. Contract written into SKILL.md (the slide contract read every Phase 7) and render.py's declaration comment.
why: Run No.29's slides 05 and 06 declared the deck's central wordless claim and authored both probe rectangles from the STORYBOARD'S CAMERA ARITHMETIC instead of measuring them off a render		revert the upgrade(2026-08-08) commit. scripts		THE HOUSE DATE FORM NOW SEES THE REST OF THE COPY, NOT JUST THE CAPTION. New `caption_check.py --copy out/<date>/copy.json` runs the EXISTING DATE_FORMS table over copy.json's reader-facing prose: document_title, post_copy, deck_summary_line, first_comment and every slide kicker, headline and label string. No new rule is introduced; this widens an existing gate to the surfaces CLAUDE.md always named it for. URLs are stripped before matching so no rule can fire inside a link, and every hit is reported rather than the first only. editor_notes_for_email, aftercare and caption_meta are deliberately OUT of scope with the reason written into the code: they are addressed to the maintainer in the dated draft, never to a reader, and gating a private note on public house style would train the machine to route around the gate. A --copy path that cannot be read is a FAIL, the same rule this file already applies to a missing --ledger and an unreadable brand.yaml. The failures land in caption_report.json, which gate_status.py already reads, so the completion gate picks them up with no change to gate_status.py; Phase 6 of routine_instructions.md now calls it after the style_lint pre-flight.
